messages.subject: time series questions
parts:
I am running a binomial model with an AR1 process as a random effect. It runs fine when left unconstrained, but crashes when constrained, even when I limit the sample size. Is there any reason why a constrained AR1 process would be a problem in a binomial model?  Does it require a particularly informative prior? 

The error message is below:

	GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [1]
	Reason    : Alloc failed
	Message   : Fail to calloc nmemb=18446744072088931588 elements of size=8 bytes
	Function  : inla_make_constraint2
	File      : src/inla.c
	Line      : 17526
	GitID     : 1f6a39183ef43d8ef33f10ff3f04fd13f8432758 - Mon Feb 22 21:27:50 2021 +0300

Aborted (core dumped)
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

I get the same error message in Windows and on Linux, with `ar1` and `rw1`, with a thousand rows or thousands of rows, which suggests to me something more fundamental is at work, perhaps a mistake I am making.

The current specification I am using is:

f(time, replicate = factor_x, model="ar1", hyper = list(prec = list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(1,.01))), initial=c(2.3, 3.7), constr = TRUE)

Thanks,
Jonathan

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] time series questions
parts:
when you have replications, the constraint is also replicated, to one
constraint pr replicate.

if the length of the time-series is N and the the number of replicates
are R, then you'll need O(N*R^2) storage to represent the joint
constraint (the constraint is stored in dense format..., not particular
smart if R is huge, since most of that matrix will be zeros)


I can check if you send me an example code
